entities.name: Cuneiform Writing
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The world's earliest writing system, developed in southern Mesopotamia (Sumer) c. 3400–3200 BCE, initially for administrative record-keeping. Evolved from pictographic tokens to wedge-shaped (Latin: cuneus, "wedge") impressions on wet clay tablets made with a reed stylus. Over three millennia, cuneiform was adapted to write Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian, Assyrian, Elamite, Hittite, Hurrian, and Urartian, serving as the writing system of an entire civilization complex. Deciphered in the 1850s by Henry Rawlinson using the trilingual Behistun Inscription.
